source.title: On the Learning Dynamics of Deep Neural Networks
source.citation: Rémi Tachet Des Combes et al., 2018
source.authors: Rémi Tachet Des Combes; M. Pezeshki; S. Shabanian; Aaron C. Courville; Yoshua Bengio

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes training classification dynamics and reports a classification experiment, but uses a different method and highly restricted settings from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The theory assumes linearly separable binary data and, for closed-form results, often one repeated vector per class. The cats-and-dogs experiment changes image brightness by class; cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The VGG16-like convolutional classifier trained with Adam reaches 100% training accuracy on brightness-modified cats-and-dogs images, testing V1's training-fit behavior in a new setting. The theoretical confidence dynamics do not measure the versions' specified effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's numerical summary is accurate but omits the central conclusion: frequent informative features can suppress learning of rarer informative features, potentially helping generalization while harming transfer. The authors also derive restricted confidence dynamics, characterize initialization failure regions, and find faster convergence with hinge loss than cross-entropy.
record.recipe_differences: The theory uses continuous-time dynamics under strong separability and initialization assumptions. The empirical experiment uses Adam on brightness-modified cats-and-dogs images rather than the benchmark and recipe described in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization region changes whether the theoretical model learns; class frequency and input norm affect theoretical convergence speed.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricted ReLU models exhibit sigmoid-shaped confidence dynamics and initialization regions where learning freezes or true-class confidence approaches 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In separable binary classification models, initialization can determine confidence dynamics and whether gradient training solves the task.

fits_no_version.finding: The classifier achieves 100% accuracy on modified test images but 43.2% on untouched test images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training with a perfectly discriminative brightness feature can produce poor transfer when that feature is removed.

fits_no_version.finding: Under restrictive theoretical assumptions, hinge loss reaches its target faster than cross-entropy, and deeper networks can learn faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss choice and depth affect convergence speed in separable models with specially structured initialization.

record.problems: The paper calls its setup extremely simplifying: the main closed-form analysis assumes a single repeated vector per class, and the data are assumed linearly separable. The empirical classification experiment modifies the images to encode class in brightness and reports no uncertainty or control comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Related-work results cited from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; explicitly random initialization; model-size comparisons; early stopping; regularized recipes.
Teacher-student realizability, spurious-minimum frequencies under standard initialization, and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training-error degradation in deep batch-normalized convolutional networks and comparisons with identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, preservation of signals and gradients across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable convolutional depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature evolution, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Its toy-model initialization failures do not qualify the convolutional training-fit result. The depth analysis lacks the batch-normalized convolutional and shortcut comparisons required by V3.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, varying model size, early stopping, or the listed regularized recipes. The empirical classification task uses class-correlated brightness changes.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical continuous-time gradient training with binary cross-entropy under the assumptions of Theorem 3.2.

conditions.value: each class contains the same vector repeated |Dk| times

rows.measure: Classification confidence follows a sigmoid and tends to 1 for the correctly classified class.
rows.note: A restricted theoretical result, not an empirical benchmark or a reported finite-time training-error value.
rows.check: This is an asymptotic confidence result for a restricted two-neuron fully connected model under gradient flow, not training classification error in a sufficiently large convolutional network. Under H2–H3, the examples already have correctly signed logits at initialization.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical continuous-time gradient training with binary cross-entropy from initializations in the failure region.

conditions.value: top-left red region of the phase diagram; y0 = -||x||z0 or y0 < -||x||z0

rows.measure: Classification confidence on the true class.
rows.value: confidence tends to 0.5, or learning stops when the neuron dies out
rows.note: Shows that training need not solve the task for these initializations; the paper does not establish how often random initialization falls in this region.
rows.check: The restricted model's confidence approaching 0.5 does not establish reversed training classification performance. Appendix A.6 explicitly keeps the true-class logit negative at every finite time. These initialization failure regions neither test V1's convolutional setting nor V4's activation-matched signal and gradient propagation mechanism.

rows.measure: Classification accuracy on the training set.
rows.note: The table reports the aggregate accuracy for the modified dataset; it does not report a CIFAR benchmark or an unmodified-data training result.
rows.check: The 100% training accuracy is correctly reported. However, 12,500 images per class describes the dataset; the paper does not specify the training split size or the classifier's initialization.
